title: Memory with mmap
description:
Write `sum_squares(n)` that gets memory from the kernel with the `mmap` system call (anonymous, private, readable and writable), stores the squares 1², 2², ..., n² in it as qwords, adds them up by reading the memory back, gives the memory back with `munmap`, and returns the sum.

- If `mmap` fails (it does for `n` = 0, since a length of 0 is invalid), return −1.
- Remember: the fourth argument goes in `r10`, and `syscall` changes `rcx` and `r11`.

| call | rax | rdi | rsi | rdx | r10 | r8 | r9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mmap | 9 | 0 | bytes | 3 | 0x22 | −1 | 0 |
| munmap | 11 | address | bytes | | | | |

solution.solution.asm:
sum_squares:
        push    rbx
        push    r12
        push    r13
        mov     r12, rdi                ; n
        lea     r13, [rdi*8]            ; bytes
        mov     eax, 9
        xor     edi, edi
        mov     rsi, r13
        mov     edx, 3
        mov     r10d, 0x22
        mov     r8, -1
        xor     r9d, r9d
        syscall
        test    rax, rax
        js      .fail
        mov     rbx, rax                ; the memory
        xor     ecx, ecx
.fill:  cmp     rcx, r12
        jge     .filled
        lea     rax, [rcx + 1]
        imul    rax, rax
        mov     [rbx + rcx*8], rax
        inc     rcx
        jmp     .fill
.filled:
        xor     edx, edx                ; the sum
        xor     ecx, ecx
.add:   cmp     rcx, r12
        jge     .added
        add     rdx, [rbx + rcx*8]
        inc     rcx
        jmp     .add
.added: push    rdx
        mov     eax, 11
        mov     rdi, rbx
        mov     rsi, r13
        syscall
        pop     rax
        jmp     .out
.fail:  mov     rax, -1
.out:   pop     r13
        pop     r12
        pop     rbx
        ret

hints: Check `rax` right after `mmap` with `test rax, rax` / `js`: a failure is a small negative number (lesson 8.04).
Keep the address, the count and the size in callee-saved registers (pushed at the start), because `syscall` changes `rcx` and `r11` and you call it twice.
rules: Use the mmap and munmap system calls.
unitTests:
test "small"
    sum_squares(1) == 1
    sum_squares(3) == 14
    sum_squares(10) == 385
test "large: 800 KB of memory"
    sum_squares(100000) == 333338333350000
test "failure"
    sum_squares(0) == -1

rules.message: Use the mmap and munmap system calls.
